name: calibration-priors
label: Parameters of the population calibration, their bounds and priors (M5 plan, Task 5.10)

rate_per_year.citation: The growth rate r of data/remodeling/growth.json; no excerpt gave a human value, so a wide log-uniform prior over five decades.

lid_pressure_scale.citation: Multiplier on the lid pressure of data/eyelid/shaw-2010.json. sigmaLn 0.7 (a factor of 2 at one SD): Shaw et al. report 8.0 +/- 3.4 mmHg between subjects and 3.8 to 55 mmHg between estimation methods (excerpt).

eom_tone_scale.citation: Multiplier on the muscle forces in equilibrium (length-proxy activation x capacity). sigmaLn 0.7: the equilibrium alone changes primary-gaze forces by about half (data/results/README.md), and the capacities are partly assumed.

stiffness_age_slope.citation: Per-year exponent of the age stiffening above the table's lower clamp age (data/materials ageStiffening.ratePerYear, from Elsheikh et al. 2007 by excerpt); the stiffness at the rigidity calibration's age (70) stays at the calibrated value, so the slope changes only the age dependence. SD 0.01: the excerpt gave group means only.

baseline_j0_mean.citation: Nuisance: mean J0 of the cohort at the baseline age (the SyntEyes stand-in, data/synteyes); fitted mainly by the youngest axis-class band. Lower bound widened from -0.5 to -1.0 D in M6 (plan Task 6.6): at -0.5 the least-squares optimum sat on the bound (M5), trading against the lid pressure (correlation -0.72); with -1.0 or -1.5 it lies inside, at -0.72 D with the lid pressure 3.5 times the table (1.8 prior SDs, about 28 mmHg, inside the 3.8-55 mmHg of Shaw et al.'s methods), cost 45.5 against 46.6. No source bounds the unloaded baseline (SyntEyes is a stand-in), so the bound is set not to bind.

baseline_j_sd.citation: Nuisance: SD of J0 and J45 at the baseline age (isotropic); sets the share of astigmatic eyes.

homeostatic_ratio.citation: Not fitted (M5 plan, Task 5.10 notes): the homeostatic offset drives axisymmetric growth and so changes only the spherical equivalent, whose adult trajectory is dominated by the crystalline lens, which the mechanical model does not contain; with the astigmatism targets alone it is unidentified. h = 1 makes the pressurized eye of the reference age homeostatic.

nearHours.citation: assumption: daily near-work hours spread evenly between 0 and 8 across the cohort (the populations' near work is not reported in the target sources).

effectiveSampleSize.citation: assumption: the target sources are summaries without sample sizes in the excerpts; 200 astigmatic eyes per band gives a binomial standard error of about 0.035 on a proportion.

classification.citation: numerical: logistic smoothing widths of the astigmatism threshold (D) and of the axis-class boundaries (in cos 2*axis), so the least-squares objective is differentiable; reported proportions use hard classes.
